It’s no secret that Heated Rivalry is one of the biggest book-to-screen adaptations of recent years. The smutty, queer hockey romance stole the hearts of fans everywhere when it was released in late 2025, and its popularity hasn’t wavered at all. Fans are only going to get more intense now that news has dropped that Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie will be suiting up for a third season as well. However, I'm concerned about one detail.

Fans of Heated Rivalry have already known about Season 2 kicking off production, as photos from the set have been leaked despite the show’s creator, Jacob Tierney, kindly asking fans to give them space while filming. The news about a third season has been highly speculated, and now, that has been confirmed as well. Both seasons are reportedly being filmed back-to-back. This theoretically means that there shouldn’t be a huge wait between seasons, and maybe fans could get all twelve episodes sometime next year.

In addition to two more seasons with Shane and Ilya, Deadline reports that Tierney is working on a standalone theatrical release that the trade believes will be a “Christmas special” or “holiday-themed episode” centered around Season 1, Episode 3 couple Scott (François Arnaud) and Kip (Robbie G.K.). It’s not the Heated Rivalry-centric bonus episode fans have been hoping for, but the holiday special could be inspired by the short holiday story author Rachel Reid penned for the couple and earlier this year took down from her official website.

As a fan of the sports drama series, I’m overjoyed at the news, but I do have one concern heading into these news seasons when it comes to what it might mean for Shane and Ilya’s relationship.

Unlike the other couples in Reid’s Game Changers book universe, Shane and Ilya’s relationship unfolds over several books. When the series was released (and subsequently renewed for a second and a secret third season), the couple’s second book, The Long Game, was the final installment in their relationship. But then Reid announced she was writing a third book, Unrivaled, centered on the fan-favorite couple.

Had Reid not made the announcement that she was writing Unrivaled, I would have confidently said that Tierney and the creative team behind Heated Rivalry planned to split The Long Game into two seasons. This would allow the show to really dig deep into Shane and Ilya’s relationship challenges and give fans a faithful adaptation like the first season did. It would also provide space for the show to explore some of the other couples in the Game Changes universe, which seems to be happening based on casting announcements for Season 2.

Splitting The Long Game into two seasons might still be the case, which is great news for fans of the novel; however, it does raise concerns about the potential for an adaptation of Unrivaled. After all, if Seasons 2 and 3 are centered on the second novel, then the show would need to be renewed for a fourth season in order to see the third book and the presumed conclusion of Shane and Ilya’s love story on screen.

Given the show’s popularity, a hypothetical fourth season seems like a no-brainer, but one also has to consider the schedules of the cast and crew. With Storrie and Williams both cast in new shows and movies, it might be hard to get them on board for another season beyond these next two. Still, I’d like to believe that the talented actors would be eager to see Ilya and Shane's storyline through to the end.

All of this is purely speculation, as we don't know much about Season 2 of Heated Rivalry other than it's expected to drop in Spring 2027. When that happens, we'll know what to expect from Season 3. Until then, I’ll be streaming, or as fans have dubbed it “reheating,” Season 1 of Heated Rivalry with my HBO Max subscription. Fans can also catch the episodes playing for a limited time in theaters in the US and Canada.

#3703. Has The Ocarina Of Time Remake Changed Too Much? Fans Debate Difficulty, Tone, And Handholding

As is often the case when something is remade, the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is generating a lot of comparisons to the original. Purists will often deride any changes made to the thing they grew up with, so I was prepared for a lot of the discussion to come off like an old man yelling at cloud about how one of the most widely celebrated video games of all time was better âback in his day.â However, the Ocarina of Time remake isnât just getting a lot of the usual remake criticism that tends to revolve around things like graphical fidelity and art style; thereâs also a fair bit of discussion about how its modern game design sensibilities may have sanded off some edges and, in so doing, diminished certain things that made Ocarina of Time great.

This morning, I came across a 16-minute video in which Twitter user KloverKlub14 rattled off most of their complaints about the remake. Some of them can be dismissed as nitpicking small details that only the sickest of sickos would ever recognize, but thereâs actually a fair bit here that stood out to me about how much easier Ocarina of Time is on Switch 2 than it ever was on the Nintendo 64.

I compiled most of my complaints with the Ocarina remake into this video pic.twitter.com/tnnNx9Jslc

— KloverKlub (@KloverKlub14) November 8, 2026

In the flood of complaints, a theme emerges. The difficulty nerf isnât as easy to sum up as saying âLink does more damage than before,â but instead manifests in several little things that add up across the course of the game. Certain environmental hazards are gone, Link no longer lands on a lower floor if he plummets off certain platforms but instead just respawns where he fell from, some enemy behaviors like Stalfos being able to revive themselves if you donât defeat an entire squad of them quickly enough have been removed, and some secrets in the environment are now signposted with elements like dedicated targets for Link to aim the Hookshot at, denying players the pleasure of figuring it out for themselves (or sparing them the effort, depending on how you feel about the change).

âPeople keep pointing at better controls and âit was harder for you before because you were a child,â conveniently ignoring that people continued to replay this game into their adulthood,â a redditor writes. âBut it goes beyond that, for both the puzzle and navigation aspect and combat, there are factually things that make it easier. Some dungeon challenges are simplified, objects in the room are less hidden and easier to spot, there’s constant exposition for what you’re supposed to do, challenges that used to be timed now no longer have a timer. Some enemies are easier, some are actually harder, like the Redeads now being more aggressive and able to run. Those changes can be subjective, but there are also changes that objectively make it easier, like Stalfos dealing half the damage they used to. On the other hand, I’ve noticed heart drops are more scarce, and I’ve never seen enemies drop three hearts like they frequently did in the original. Other examples are King Dodongo now being less of a joke, since you can no longer just stand to the side as he rolls past you, and he now also summons baby dodongos. But then there’s bosses like Phantom Ganon who is significantly easier with the slow moving energy balls.â

Finished Ocarina remake. Pretty conflicted overall. I think this is a death by a thousand cuts situation honestly. There are too many little things that I loved about the original game that have been lost here.

Something Iâve definitely noticed is that some parts of the Ocarina of Time remake feel like theyâre shying away from the darkness of the original game. Yes, I am comparing the level of dread and fear I felt playing the game as a kid to what I feel now as an adult, but Iâm specifically thinking of the original gameâs more explicit references to the violent deaths of people who arenât villains. One notable example that a lot of fans have pointed out is that at the end of the gameâs first act, when Zelda has fled Castle Town and Ganondorf has gone after her, thereâs a soldier who can be found in the back alleys of the town that was originally mortally wounded. The original Ocarina of Time made it pretty clear that he had died from his injuries trying to save Zelda, with the text after his dying words saying âheâs not moving anymore,â but that text no longer appears in the remake. Instead, you can talk to this man as many times as you want.

I found the solider! pic.twitter.com/Y0ZUFVlqBB

— Steve (@StupidhanyEne) November 5, 2026

Another thing Iâve seen circulating is that some believed blood stains that appeared throughout the Shadow Temple had been removed, as you no longer see the blood-red puddles underneath what look like crucifixes. However, as others have pointed out, old, dried blood wouldnât retain the same crimson color that fresh blood does, so the darker smears that appear in the remake are actually more accurate.

I suspect the young development team wanted to bring back the bloodstains in the OoT well, but were probably told no.

The result was probably this middle ground of very old stains, just not red. #Zelda pic.twitter.com/SKUsUshcMZ

— Mighty (@MightyGazelle1) November 6, 2026

âItâs funny how the more realistic implementation of this with faded dry blood is easier to sneak into an E10 game because it can be passed off as dirt or rust,â a fan writes on Reddit. âThe bright red blood of the OG isâ¦ bloodier, obviously, but arguably more cartoony.â

These are smaller details, but thereâs also a pretty major scene in the endgame that no longer includes a character coughing up blood. To avoid spoilers, weâll just link the comparison here if you want to click on it. Given how much more detailed Ocarina of Time looks on the Switch 2, itâs possible Nintendo omitted this to avoid a T for Teen rating with the ESRB. Most Zelda games are either rated E or E10+, with the exception of Twilight Princess, which got a T rating back in 2006 and is widely considered the âdarkestâ game in the series.

While changes are a big part of the conversation, another is whether or not Nintendo played it too safe when remaking Ocarina of Time. One major point of contention is that Hyrule Field, the overworld players pass through as they head from one town to the next, feels just as empty as it did on the N64, though some donât think it needed to get peppered with enemies and activities,Â

âBack in 1998, Hyrule Field was a nice little tech demo that allowed Nintendo to show off how the N64 could render some really big triangles, just to make the poor old PlayStation look bad,â Moon Game Studios CEO Thomas Mahler says on Twitter. âBut from a design perspective, it was already pretty lousy back then. And to simply copy that design 1:1 today? Nah. Every designer at Nintendo should be crying foul and know that this could be done so much better nowadays.â

not to be a hater or maybe itâs a bad cIip, but there just being Iike a giant empty fieId with Iike nothing going on feeIs so sIoppish to me.whyâs everything gotta be boring open worId slop https://t.co/RpX8VuzXdd

— toby (@The_Bees_Sneeze) November 9, 2026

âI think Hyrule Field being largely empty allows the world to breathe and gives the game a sense of scale and immersion,â New Blood Interactiveâs Mark Diaz argues. âPlayers don’t always need to be bombarded with activities, sometimes it’s nice to just exist in the game world and be alone with your thoughts. I grew up in the middle of nowhere in North Carolina. In real life, nature is like that sometimes, just a lot of trees and grass and rocks and leaves, with nothing particularly important or interesting going on, and that’s okay! Hyrule Field felt familiar to me in that way.â

Overall, the Ocarina of Time remake is an interesting case study in both how much and how little game design has changed in the years since the original. Is it a solid way to experience one of the most beloved games of all time, or does it feel like a sanitized replica of something that didnât need to be modernized in this way? Or is it just kind of a cool thing to exist that doesnât have any bearing on your feelings on the original and brings a special game to a new audience? Thatâs in the eye of the beholder, I suppose.Â

What this does make me very curious about is how Nintendo might handle a hypothetical Majoraâs Mask remake. That game has a lot more friction and challenging systems than Ocarina of Time, and I wonder if Nintendo might excise some of those for a modern audience. There are hints that such a remake might be coming in the future, but thereâs been no official announcement as of right now.

#3702. See Stephen Colletti and Wife Alex Weaver's 1st Holiday Card With Baby

Stephen Colletti and his wife, Alex Weaver, are celebrating their first holiday season as parents — and they have the adorable card to prove it.

The couple teamed up with Minted to commemorate the special occasion, and Us can exclusively reveal their Coastal Stripe foil-pressed holiday card by artist Stephanie Heinrich Godbout.

“I wanted something casual, I wanted blue and something that felt true to us. I also wanted a sunset,” Weaver, 32, told Us of her vision for the card and accompanying photo shoot. “I was a little nervous about how the shoot would go with a baby close to bedtime, but it actually went surprisingly well. Rhodes is such a happy baby, which made it easy and fun!”

Signed from mom, dad, baby and their Siamese cat, Bennet, the stunning light blue striped card features a gold accent border and a dreamy black-and-white photo of the family of three, with baby Rhodes sitting atop Colletti’s shoulders as Weaver holds her husband’s hand.

The NASCAR reporter and Colletti, 40, announced the arrival of their first child, son Rhodes August Colletti, via Instagram in May after tying the knot the previous October.

The Laguna Beach alum reflected with Us on sharing this new chapter with fans who have followed his journey since his early reality TV days.

“Becoming a dad has been the most meaningful change of my life, and the kindness people have shown us in this new chapter has meant so much,” he told Us. “It’s pretty wild that people who first met me as an insecure, knucklehead kid are still here cheering me on. In a way, we’ve grown up together.”

The couple — who celebrated their first wedding anniversary with a kid-free trip to New York City, where Colletti surprised Weaver with Harry Styles tickets — are still adjusting to life as parents, and discovering new surprises each step of the way.

“How little sleep you get and how much my life revolves around my baby’s sleep,” Weaver told Us of the most surprising part of becoming a mom, adding, “I’ve also learned how much coffee one person can drink in a day!”

As for Colletti, the One Tree Hill alum told Us he was surprised to learn “that bouncing on a pink yoga ball while holding a baby at 3 in the morning would be a massive part of early fatherhood. I will never look at a yoga ball the same again.”

Yet, Weaver reiterated that it’s all worth it.

“Rhodes is the best boy,” she told Us. “He’s so happy, so sweet and curious. He amazes us every day with something. It’s been so fun watching his little personality develop.”

As the holiday season approaches, Colletti and Weaver are looking forward to introducing Rhodes to their favorite traditions — and making a few of their own.

“On Christmas morning, my mom always makes cinnamon rolls, so I’m excited to carry that tradition on with Rhodes. This year, Santa will be making his first delivery of goodies for him, which makes everything feel even more special,” Weaver told Us. “We also got new family stockings with Rhodes’ monogram, so it’ll be fun to start creating little traditions of our own as a family.”

Since they both spend a lot of time on the road for work, Weaver and Colletti are looking forward to a “cozy” holiday at home with their baby boy.

“I know he’s going to grow up so quickly, so I’m trying to soak up as much of this stage as I can,” she told Us. “I want to bottle it up and keep it forever.”

#3701. Sam Rockwell Breaks Down Scenes From His Career, Including ‘Charlie’s Angels’ and ‘The White Lotus’

“Thank God for Marvin Gaye and this song,” Sam Rockwell says while watching a younger version of himself dance opposite a stunned Drew Barrymore in the 2000 action-comedy Charlie’s Angels. “I mean, this song really makes the scene.”

While telling stories from his more than 35-year career across film and television for Vanity Fair’s Scene Selection, Rockwell says people tried to stop him from appearing in the remake of the 1970s TV series starring Barrymore, Cameron Diaz, and Lucy Liu. When he joined the project as secretly evil software engineer Eric Knox—who starts the film as Barrymore’s love interest—the script was “a work in progress,” Rockwell recalls. “A lot of people told me not to do this movie. And then, they all ate their words. It had a very specific kind of popcorn vibe to it, very unique, and I don’t think I’ve seen [it] since.”

Rockwell originally envisioned a more “punk rock” direction for his character, but changed his approach after speaking with friend and former Galaxy Quest costar Alan Rickman. “You know, Sam, keep it simple,” Rockwell recalled the late actor telling him. “When I did Die Hard, I killed someone and ate a sandwich.”

Over the decades, Rockwell tried his hand at a mix of projects—somber indies like sci-fi drama Moon (2009), studio awards contenders including The Green Mile (1999), and mainstream fare like Iron Man 2 (2010). “I was dating Leslie Bibb when Iron Man one came out…. It sort of changed superhero movies,” says Rockwell, whose now real-life partner of nearly 20 years appeared in the first film.

After being cast in the sequel as fast-talking arms dealer Justin Hammer, Rockwell learned that he would share most of his scenes with Mickey Rourke as fellow fictional baddie and Russian physicist Ivan Vanko. “Mickey didn’t want to meet me until we were on camera,” Rockwell remembers. “It was a wild experience…. Because my scenes were dialogue-driven, whereas a lot of [the rest of] it was special effects…it was a surprisingly actor-friendly experience being that it was a studio movie for me.”

Bibb and Rockwell, who also shared scenes in Iron Man 2, reunited onscreen in 2025 for season three of The White Lotus as it was filmed in Thailand. He joined the series partway through production, tasked with performing Mike White’s “brilliant monologue” about sex addiction and gender identity opposite Walton Goggins. “Leslie helped me get off-book in South Africa; we were on safari,” says Rockwell, who says he based his searching Buddhist character, Frank, on Martin Sheen in Apocalypse Now.

The actor also detailed the past screen inspiration behind his Oscar-winning performance in Martin McDonagh’s drama, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri (2017), calling the trajectory of his role as a bigoted local cop, “[The Andy Griffith Show’s] Barney Fife becomes [Taxi Driver’s] Travis Bickle,” says Rockwell. He joins forces with McDonagh once more for the new awards-season contender Wild Horse Nine, in which he acts with teenage idol John Malkovich. “I love characters who change and are underestimated by the audience,” says Rockwell of Three Billboards. “And this is really that.”

Skydance Games has "made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Just over a month after Paramount closed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery and renamed itself as Skydance, the company's games division has laid off an unspecified number of employees.

Reports of the cuts first surfaced earlier today on LinkedIn, where multiple employees reported being let go. Lead engineer David Vera, who was not among those put out of work, said the studio "lost a ton of great talent," while another post by principal environment artist Dana Klaren listed more than 25 people who'd been let go, including himself. Senior gameplay and game AI programmer Rebecca Vessal said in her own message that "most" of her team had been let go.

Prior to their merger, both Paramount and Warner had their own game divisions: Paramount actually had two, Skydance Interactive and Skydance New Media, which were mashed together into Skydance Games Studio earlier this year. The merged company announced that it will be publishing PlatinumGames' upcoming Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin; Skydance New Media is also working on Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, although the current status of that game is unclear.

On the other side of the equation, Warner Bros. Games had struggled to follow up on the 2023 hits Legacy of Hogwarts and Mortal Kombat 1; the division was assessed as being of "relatively minor" value by Netflix when it was in the hunt for Warner, although Netflix co-CEO Gregory Peters said he was "super excited" about some of the properties the deal would provide access to.

And now, as we've seen many times previously, consolidation means cuts, which Skydance confirmed with Variety. "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business," a rep said in a statement.

"We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company."

The Indian movie features one awesome collab.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

India’s most expensive movie ever is Ramayana, which is one of the latest 2026 movie releases to hit theaters. The movie was a massive undertaking, and that's evident just by watching the trailer. All in all, the film is firmly steeped in the culture its representing. But, even though the flick was made thousands of miles from Hollywood, a producer was very much inspired by one of our greatest filmmakers, Christopher Nolan, as CinemaBlend recently learned.

Did you know that Ramayana is co-composed by Hans Zimmer? The German musician has become one of the most beloved and prolific composers of modern cinema, and that’s exactly why the movie's producer, Namit Malhotra, asked for him to come aboard the filmmaking team. Here’s how he told us the story during CB’s exclusive Ramayana interview:

I grew up in India completely fanboying on A.R. Rahman, who I absolutely love and his music has sort of formed a big part of my growing up and childhood and youth. And then, I moved to L.A. in 2010, the year Inception came out. I started to fall in love with Chris Nolan and Han Zimmer's music that was done for The Dark Knight and all the films that came subsequent to that. And, it was one of those moments when we decided to make Ramayana. I said literally as a fanboy, ‘What if I could take Han Zimmer and A.R. Rahman together and they would create a new sound, a new feeling, a new energy that the world has not heard before?’ And everybody is like, ‘Yeah, why not?’

Malhotra called himself a self-described “fanboy” of Nolan movies who's been in awe of his movies for a while. So, when he went on to make his own epic, he thought he'd take the long-shot move to try to get Zimmer on board for Ramayana alongside his favorite composer from India, A.R. Rahman. (Did you know Zimmer actually helped convince Nolan to make Interstellar, by the way? A greatly overlooked detail is just how important musicians like him are pivotal to the filmmaking process.) As Malhotra added:

One thing I learned in America, there's no harm in asking because the worst you'll be told is ‘No’. That's not how we grew up in India. Like you normally don't ask the question if you think the answer is no.

Even though Namit Malhotra had never met Zimmer and didn't know would react to the request, the producer took “a cue from [his] American friends” and reached out to the Interstellar composer. This is what happened next:

I made a pitch and a presentation to him. I couldn't have been more surprised by his intellect, his intuitive judgment because he was like, ‘Namit, you don't have to sell me on Ramayana. If something has existed in the world for over 5,000 years and generation after generation, more people are excited to consume it, learn from it, and it's still not lost its relevance, there must be more than what you and I can understand. So we should just figure out how we do this and not worry about whether we should do it.’

Ramayana Is Making A Huge Global Push. I Still Can't Tell From Reviews What I'm Getting Into

The idea really does sell itself, doesn’t it? Ramayana is a Hindu epic poem that’s very central to India’s culture. It has inspired the celebrations of Diwali and Dussehra, and the story also serves as a moral cornerstone as well. It focuses on two characters: Rama and Ravana. Prince Rama is the seventh incarnation / avatar of Lord Vishnu, who becomes responsible for taking down King Ravana from having uncontrollable power over people. It's India's own classic good vs. evil story, and it has really stood the test of time.

I'm no sure how aware Zimmer was of the legend of Ramayana before it was pitched to him, yet he was apparently sold quite quickly. He got the importance of it being told for the big screen. Malhotra told us that Zimmer’s reaction to his pitch even “revalidated” his own reasons to make it and “reinvigorated [his] own confidence” since he respects the composer so much.

Hans Zimmer is a busy musical savant, who’s recently worked on the Dune movies and the upcoming Harry Potter TV series, so he could have easily passed, but he clearly didn’t want to. And, as a result of his participation, one of Hollywood's best got to put his mark on a historical Indian film. You can hear Zimmer’s original music for Ramayana, which is playing in theaters around the world right now.

#3698. 25 Hours With World Of Warcraft: Forever

World of WarcraftWorld of Warcraft: Forever

Here are some things I have done in the 25 hours I have played of World of Warcraft: Forever so far:

Sound awful? Well…maybe. When I think about how I could be spending that time finally weeding my garden, or doing all the real-life chores I keep putting off, yeah. Bit of a waste of time. Such a waste of time, in fact, that I have hardly even touched most of the new content in WoW: Forever. I did play the Skyborne in beta: their starting island is fine. A bit too modern-feeling for me, but fine. I’ve definitely encountered a few new quests mixed in here and there, and the aforementioned torch and sleeping bag missions were new as well (though I did the former in beta and the latter in Season of Discovery already). But I haven’t even touched the new dungeons. I’m months away (at my current pace) from the new raids. I’m not even a high enough level to check out the Riverlands yet. May as well be playing Classic, right?

But as I hike back and forth and up and down Azeroth, I tilt my camera around. That draw distance! I see Mt. Hyjal, misty, looming in the distance, waiting for me at max level. The sun rises and sets over plains and swamps. It filters through trees and fog. I /wave at the other travelers I meet on the road. I sit at campfires and chat with others who gather around. People buff me with their class’ spells when they see me, or resurrect me if they see my dead body so that I don’t have to struggle all the way back to it. One person yesterday finished a quest just as I was starting, and volunteered to stick around (wasting 20 more minutes of their own time) to help me finish too. Another time, the game’s layer system goofed while I was on a zeppelin and something like 200 of us all ran into Undercity at once, prompting humorous panic from the folks already inside. Today, myself and two others started an entire, lengthy conversation in our zone’s general chat while I was squeezing in some early morning fishing time, just by saying “Good morning” in hopes someone would say it back. It ended with someone telling us all silly, made-up stories about a warlock named Daniel.

Somehow, this time doesn’t feel like such a waste anymore. It’s…soothing, I think. The slowness, the friction. A lot of this was always present in WoW Classic, sure. But I think the little added touches in Foreverâthe extra quests for things like torches and sleeping bags, the campfires, the layering ensuring that my world is always packed with other peopleâare lending the experience some new magic that wasn’t there before. In the past, the slowness of Classic felt more like a product of the time we were in, because no one had streamlined MMORPGs to eliminate it yet. But Forever embraces that pace and leans into it as a design feature rather than a flaw, making those moments feel rewarding on purpose rather than on occasional accident. More often than ever, you’re put in positions where there’s nothing to do but say hello to other people and forge a brief connection, or to sit back and admire the way the new lighting plays on the ripples in the river. It’s WoW, but with mindfulness. And mindfulness is something I’ve been in desperate want of lately.

Given that, it’s been really, really hard for me to put World of Warcraft: Forever down, even in the face of another brilliant game launch happening simultaneously. In my brain, a task list has populated of things I want to do: a dozen or so quests, of course, plus that one extra quest I have to turn in on the other continent, and that sleeping bag scavenger hunt I’m in the middle of. I need to visit my class trainer back in Orgrimmar or Thunder Bluff here soon to learn some new skills, and also all the profession trainers, and also the bank. There are some dungeons I’d like to run soon. All of this backs up in my brain the same way my real-life chores list does, but with the distinguishing feature that I dread none of it. I am eager to take part in every aspect, even though over half of these will inevitably be time-consuming, even time-wasting affairs. I’ll get to level 60 eventually, but I’m in no hurry to do it. To my editors: I’m sorry I’m inevitably going to take so long with this review. But there are so many wonderful, pointless distractions between here and there, I can’t help but let myself be blissful and slightly bored for another 50 or more hours first.

#3697. 2026 Kids Choice Awards Participants Revealed

Some of Hollywood’s brightest stars are preparing to survive the slime at the 2026 Kids Choice Awards.

Us can exclusively reveal that Teyana Taylor, Keke Palmer, Tony Hawk and Matthew Gray Gubler will all participate in the Saturday, November 14, award ceremony among the star-studded attendees. Zombies costars Milo Manheim and Meg Donnelly will also be present for the 2026 KCAs.

Palmer, 33, is nominated for Favorite Podcast for her “Baby, It’s Keke” show, alongside “Anything Goes With Emma Chamberlain,” “Avatar: Braving the Elements,” “Hey Jonas,” “LOL Podcast,” “New Heights With Jason and Travis Kelce,” “Percy Jackson and the Olympians Official Podcast” and “Stuff You Should Know.”

Manheim, 25, and Donnelly, 26, meanwhile, will be celebrating their Disney Channel movie Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires, which scored a nod in the Watch Party category alongside A Very Jonas Christmas Movie, Camp Rock 3, Clash of the Thundermans, Descendants: Wicked World and Dora and the Search for Sol Dorado.

Donnelly and Manheim, who are no strangers to the KCAs stage, wrapped up their roles of Addison and Zed in Zombies 4.

“I think our characters have honestly changed so much because we’ve gotten so much older,” Donnelly exclusively told Us in July 2025. “I think these movies have happened through every formative year of our lives. … Those were, like, massive years of a human’s life and so, I feel like we’ve seen each other in so many different seasons of our lives and it’s really cool.”

Of course, Donnelly and Manheim are far from the 2026 participants with KCAs history.

Taylor, 35, previously attended the 2015 Kids’ Choice Sports Awards, while Gubler’s animated film Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel won Favorite Movie in 2009. Hawk, 58, for his part, is a fixture at the KCAs, where he has taken home multiple blimps, been slimed and performed live stunts. The skateboarder showed off his skills during a live demo during the 2025 ceremony alongside young athlete Katelyn West.

“I don’t have any great aspirations these days. Everything I do now is kind of a side mission,” Hawk quipped during a red carpet interview last year. “And they’re always fun. I never expected any of this anyway, so it’s all a nice surprise.”

At the time, Hawk ruminated on his legacy in sport, adding, “Hopefully as someone who raised the profile of skateboarding as best I could and provided more places to do it.”

Saturday’s KCAs will be hosted by Grammy nominee Alex Warren, who will also be on hand to present the iconic King of Comedy Award to Chris Pratt.

#3696. The Curious Case of Olivia Reingold’s AI Photo at a Democratic Victory Party: Valentino, Chanel, and a Free Press Mystery

On Monday night, the eve of the 2026 midterm elections, the fashion crowd celebrated at the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards, colloquially referred to as the Oscars of American fashion. Tory Burch was honored with the Positive Change Award, which was presented to her by Anna Wintour, the global editorial director of Vogue and chief content officer of Condé Nast. In her remarks, Wintour made the evening’s only direct reference to the midterms, reminiscing about attending a fundraising event for James Talarico, who successfully flipped Texas in the race for the Senate last night, alongside Burch. After applause from the audience, Wintour, a prolific Democratic fundraiser herself, looked up and addressed the room: “Let’s hope all of Texas feels the way you do,” she said.

The American fashion crowd has largely distanced itself from politics since the 2024 election. During their time in the White House as first ladies, Michelle Obama and Jill Biden were staunch supporters of the American fashion industry, often wearing American designers for public appearances. Melania Trump, in contrast, has more often preferred European labels. It’s an MO that trickles down into the political parties they represent.

There were many headlines that came out of last night’s midterms: Talarico flipped Texas, Annie Andrews flipped South Carolina, New Hampshire’s Chris Pappas became the first out gay man to be elected to the Senate, and Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia and Deb Haaland of New Mexico became the first Black and Native American women, respectively, to be elected governor in the history of the US.

And yet it wasn’t just good news (and many great memes) that circulated in my group chats last night; there were also some fashion choices worth noting. First, the most pressing: Where were Steve Kornacki’s khakis? And what was the reasoning behind Haley Stevens’s ludicrously capacious hat? Some questions in life simply go unanswered.

Kornacki, a national political correspondent for NBC News, does not make his political affiliations public. But men in his age range (he is 47) and in the generations that follow—millennials and Gen Z—have been contending with what formalwear means and signals today.

Democratic men have been hard at work on their public image since the 2024 election, largely distancing themselves from the MAGA look and its too-large suits and extra-wide ties. In separating themselves from the manosphere, men like Abdul El-Sayed, who won the Senate race in Michigan, and Jon Ossoff, who was reelected to the Senate in Georgia, have been dressing more like the less buttoned up, progressive men they represent and less like the old establishment politicians on both the right and the left.

On the campaign trail, El-Sayed often sported tees and sweaters rather than button-downs and ties, frequently wearing taut sweaters and henleys under his suit jacket, while Ossoff largely opted for rolled cuffs and no jacket. As the two delivered victory speeches last night, they each wore a tailored suit—a little too tight in the arms; these are men who seem to eat their fair share of protein—and ditched their tie.

It’s a familiar image of a more laid-back look, but one in stark contrast to that of the faces of the right: Donald Trump, JD Vance, et al. Ossoff and El-Sayed, similarly to Kamala Harris during her presidential bid, also leaned into what was happening on the internet. These days, netizens are happy to objectify men and christen a new internet boyfriend every week. Ossoff’s and El-Sayed’s campaigns seemed to understand the power of thirst—that their suits were too tight was most likely not completely intentional, but it did help underscore a simple fact: that they are fit, and that their virility can be both attractive and nonthreatening all at once.

Zohran Mamdani speaking at an event on election night. Mamdani also ditched his tie on Tuesday, in line with some of his fellow Democrats.

It is worth noting, however, that there are some men further to the left, both in politics and around it, who have reembraced the suit: Zohran Mamdani and Hasan Piker. On one hand, this has served a similar purpose as Ossoff’s and El-Sayed’s choices: It has distanced them from looksmaxxers and other conservative-leaning young men. On the other hand, a suit for Mamdani and Piker signifies what suits have always represented: that these are grown men doing important things.

The men are not the full story, however. Bottoms and Haaland came as they are, nodding to the communities they represent. The former wore a bright fuchsia suit and matching blouse, a callback to the lively and monochromatic dressing that is a deeply embedded and celebrated tradition in Black church culture. Haaland’s jewelry—firefly earrings and a beaded necklace—nodded at the style of accessories that is representative of Native style and fashion. If there is something that fashion clearly signifies, it’s community and belonging.

It is a running punch line that the left is more closely connected to fashion—it’s the wine-and-cheese crowd, the elites. (Hillary Clinton, during her bid for the presidency in 2016, was dragged online and by the press for wearing an Armani jacket that reportedly retailed for some $12,000 while delivering a speech that touched on income inequality.) While it’s true that fashion designers are often more enthusiastic about dressing progressives than they are about dressing conservatives, in the era of Trump and the MAGA look, this has become a half-baked story.

Olivia Reingold, a staff writer at The Free Press, made a post on X last night while reporting from an event for the Michigan Democratic Party. “So far at Abdul El-Sayed’s election night event I’ve spotted, Valentino heels, a Chanel bag, a Moncler jacket, Rolex watches, and a YSL bag among other designer items,” Reingold wrote, captioning an image of a woman holding a gold quilted Chanel handbag and a pair of Valentino Rockstud leather pumps.

Read Fit Check: Your front row seat to the power players, peacocks, and deep pockets of fashion—and how they influence the rest of the world.

When one takes a closer look, however, the image has several discrepancies. The style and make of the Chanel Flap bag is inconsistent with others the brand has sold, and the Valentino shoes in question appear askew in proportion; their straps have several punched holes that the authentic Valentino style does not. This could mean that the products in the image are not authentic, but there is another suggestive tell: The bottom strap on the left shoe appears to cut through its connecting strap rather than around, a classic mistake made when artificial intelligence is used to create or alter an image. A run of the image through several AI detectors, including SynthID, a digital watermarking approach created by Google DeepMind that detects media generated by OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, and Kakao, suggests the use of AI. SynthID detected that “this media was made or edited with OpenAI.” (Vanity Fair has reached out to Chanel and Valentino to advise on the authenticity of the products.)

Reingold did not reply to a request for comment, but on Thursday afternoon followed up with a new post on X, admitting to using AI “to brighten and sharpen an image of a woman in Valentino shoes and a Chanel bag.”

It’s become too easy to try to make a point about the left’s fashion choices: that Rama Duwaji, wife of Mamdani, should not wear pricey shoes, even if borrowed, because of her political beliefs; or that Democratic women should not carry Valentino or Chanel and vote for a candidate seeking to tax the wealthy. Therein lies the crux of the argument: Does this mean that luxury shoppers should align themselves with MAGA because it’s a party associated with billionaires like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos and logo-clad celebs like Nicki Minaj, who wore Chanel to the polls in New Hampshire? The answer is simple: no.

Our fashion choices say much about our values, identity, and aspirations. And while politicians have oftentimes utilized fashion to align themselves with specific groups or appear friendly to voters, they, in broad strokes, do not define our political affiliations. A Chanel bag does not make a Democrat, just as a red tie does not make a Republican.

On a call with investors today, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pushed back on the idea that PC players have a different relationship with the Grand Theft Auto series than console players.

"Your PC players seem to engage with GTA a bit differently than console," said Oppenheimer & Co analyst Martin Yang during a Q&A session. "There are roleplay options. Over time, do you think you want to close the player experience gap between console and PC, or do you view the two platforms as more independent because of their respective technical capabilities?"

Zelnick responded with acknowledgement that series like Civilization started on PC and expanded onto consoles, but said that "generally speaking, the experiences on console and PC tend to be roughly the same" and that, in general, "the capabilities of the PC platform today aren't different materially from console capabilities."

The vanilla GTA Online experience may be roughly equivalent for console and PC players, but the console versions don't have the mods that have helped keep GTA 5 relevant for 13 years. Take-Two of course knows that: It acquired the FiveM GTA 5 multiplayer mod behind so many RP servers.

Answering a related question about console jailbreaking, modding, and monetization opportunities, Zelnick said later that "the FiveM business is a profitable business," but then turned back to one of his stock lines.

"The mission of this company is to create the best entertainment on earth and bring it to consumers around the world," said the Take-Two CEO. "If we do that right, the monetization takes care of itself."

Take-Two has consistently declined to reveal anything about its plans for GTA 6 on PC or the future of GTA Online, and I didn't have high hopes that it would change tack with the console launch just over a week away, but props to the savvy investment analysts who asked about the topics anyway.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

As I think the questioner from Oppenheimer was getting at, it's sensible to wonder whether the custom servers and roleplaying features made popular by GTA 5 modders and streamers on PC will come stock in the next GTA Online iteration, including on consoles. Zelnick didn't sound particularly enthused about modding in his responses today—he said that Take-Two "isn't religious on the topic"—but I'm not reading much into it.

For now, Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching on November 19 as a singleplayer-only console game, with no PC release date announced, and no known plans to launch a new version of GTA Online set in Vice City and its surroundings, though we expect both of those things to happen eventually.

#3694. Dax Shepard Slams Rumors About 'Abusive' Relationship With Kristen Bell

Dax Shepard is fed up with the rumors surrounding his marriage to Kristen Bell.

“Another round of me being a terrible person was in the media, and like, I avoided that,” Shepard, 51, said during the Monday, November 9, episode of his “Armchair Expert” podcast. “But then it hit Kristen’s doorstep really hard, and then I got to find out everything that people are saying about me.”

The Parenthood alum then noted the “weird narrative” circulating on the internet that paints him as “controlling, abusive, now flirting with people in public, which I don’t do.”

Shepard and Bell, 46, who tied the knot in 2013, recently made headlines after the Nobody Wants This star made viral comments about her husband’s unconventional flirting method: complimenting other people.

“If we go to a dinner or something, like, there’s a couple things Dax does where he doesn’t have to look up and wink at me, but I know that he’s just being the best boy,” Bell said during the October 26 episode of Shepard’s podcast. “We’ll be at dinner, and, like, he’ll say to the waiter or waitress, he’ll go, ‘Wow, you have incredible eyelashes, gorgeous eyes, great job.’”

While Bell argued that this is a form of flirting with her because she loves seeing Shepard being kind to others, critics slammed the behavior as disrespectful and a form of emotional abuse and manipulation.

Shepard’s cohost, Monica Padman, agreed on Monday that the online discourse is “frustrating,” adding that “the internet wants a narrative” and will “find it wherever.”

Shepard said he found it disheartening to hear these rumors after growing up around abusive men himself.

“For me, growing up around certain men who behaved a certain way, and then literally dedicating my whole life to being the opposite of all that … I don’t ever yell at my children,” he added, referring to his and Bell’s daughters, Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11. “I don’t swear at them. I don’t yell at my wife. You know, like, to have given it my all to be the opposite of what now some group of people is saying I am is hard, of course. So hard. I don’t love it.”

Shepard added that he found the speculation “deeply insulting” to Bell.

“She’s, what, she’s sitting in the house with her two daughters and modeling some abusive relationship? Like, it’s very offensive to her,” he said.

Shepard also said Bell’s flirting comments were taken out of context.

“We’re saying I flirt with Kristen by tipping people a lot, and I flirt with Kristen. Yeah, by complimenting people. If you think I’m complimenting hot young waitresses, you got a problem, right?” he said. “I’m finding the dude that I don’t think has had a compliment in a while and telling him I love his shoes. It’s always somebody that I want to make their day. And so those compliments [are] flirting with Kristen.”

Shepard continued, “I will offer publicly $10 million to any server you can find that I have given my number to, or hit on.”

He concluded, “Generally, I can brush [these controversies] off, but when we’re now on year two of now, there’s a new [one] … then it just starts making me think like, ‘Oh, is this now my f***ing role going forward is just, like, every four months there’s another thing about me being a terrible man. And that makes me want to go away.”

Last year, Bell and Shepard faced controversy when the Frozen actress celebrated their 12th anniversary by recalling her husband vowing to “never kill” her despite being “heavily incentivized” to do so. Critics, including the National Network to End Domestic Violence, slammed the post for joking about domestic violence.

Back in January of this year, the couple made headlines again when Cher told Bell that she is the “better half” in her marriage to Shepard. The Zathura actor later said he thought the singer’s remark was “hysterical.”

#3693. GTA 6 Pre-Orders Are Coming In ‘Far In Excess’ Of What Take-Two Expected, Says CEO

There’s just over a week left before Grand Theft Auto 6‘s launch, and by all accounts it sounds like it’s going to be massive. It feels like GTA 6 is everywhere, and early reports have suggested that the $100 digital deluxe edition is outselling even the $80 regular version. Even the CEO of Rockstar owner Take-Two is saying he’s surprised by how well the game is selling already, claiming in the company’s quarterly earnings that its pre-orders are “tracking far above our initial expectations.”

Pre-order incentives have been plentiful in recent weeks, with Walmart offering a “surprise” of some sort, and a lot of free bonus content bundled in no matter where you buy it. Digital pre-loads begin tomorrow, but physical pre-orders are a code in a box, so you won’t be able to redeem it until the day of. Physical discs won’t be available at launch.

What’s more bonkers to me than a nebulous “exceeded expectations” on pre-orders is that GTA 5 is still selling roughly five million copies per quarter, reaching nearly 235 million copies sold in the last few months. I’ve been watching Take-Two’s earnings for years now, and I don’t think I can remember a time when GTA 5 wasn’t selling at least five million per quarter. But if there were a time for it to drop off, I’d say now would be it, given that a brand new game is coming out imminently. And yet! The franchise overall has sold nearly 480 million units.

Overall, it wasn’t aÂ greatÂ quarter for Take-Two, with net bookings down 18 percent year-over-year and net revenue down as well. Take-Two is reiterating its guidance for the year, though, of net bookings of $8 to $8.2 billion: an absolutely bonkers amount of money that can only be explained by a new GTA (net bookings were $6.72 billion last year, and $5.56 billion the year prior).

GTA 6 is, curiously, the only upcoming game in Take-Two’s pipeline that has a firm release date at the moment. 2K is preparing its slate of sports titles for next year, and Project ETHOS, BioShock, and Judas are all still in limbo. For now, everything (quite understandably) hangs on GTA 6.

Over a decade after Boy Meets World ended in 2000, a spinoff series was developed for Disney Channel and called Girl Meets World. But even after Girl ended in 2017, there were still some characters that fans wanted to see more of. That’s all the more reason I'm so excited to hear Will Friedle and Matthew Lawrence talking about their own spinoff idea. And, seriously, I need a network exec to hear them out!

Cory Matthews and Shawn Hunter may have been one of the most perfect best friend pairings, based on their exploits in Boy Meets World. However, those two characters' older brothers, Jack and Eric, are also truly a bromance deserving of attention. During a recent episode of Pod Meets World, Matthew Lawrence, who played Jack, said during a press junket that he was asked about a Jack/Eric spin-off series. Will Friedle dropped some very positive thoughts on the prospect, and they make me giddy:

I think you could still do it. Jack and Eric come together. It’s the new Odd Couple!

Yes! This needs to come together. For those who don’t know, Neil Simon’s play The Odd Couple is about two mismatched roommates, and Jack and Eric definitely fit that bill. While Jack is the logical straight man of the duo, Eric is the zany eccentric. As the two characters (and the actors who played) were so yin and yang, a spinoff would definitely make for some entertaining TV.

Lawrence went on to explain that a Jack/Eric spinoff was once in the cards, but the relationship between the creators and Disney “kind of fell apart.” Also, Lawrence recently told EW he could see the duo, both in their 40s, forced back together after going their separate ways. Lawrence continued to say on the podcast that if a potential spinoff isn’t picked up by television, he has an excellent idea of how a micro spin-off series could work, and I’m loving it:

If anything, it’s like the new YouTube in a sense that these days, as you see with Obsession and all of these things that are coming, I mean, that’s kind of the new groundlings when you talk about comedy. The new spot where they bring out shows. So maybe if we even start, maybe it’s like, build it and they will come.

It’s true that YouTube has become the new platform for creatives to bring their ideas to fruition before they hit the big or small screens. If there's enough attention, it would be so interesting to see if this possible BMW offshoot could hit streaming one day.

Friedle said himself he’s “totally down” for a spinoff, so I'm feeling somewhat hopeful that the two might try to see this through. The last time fans saw Jack’s big one-time return on Girl Meets World, he reunited with Eric. However, it was revealed that Jack was a high-ranking executive at an environmentally harmful firm, which clashed with Eric's position as a newly elected senator. However, the iconic duo mended fences at Eric’s niece’s school dance, with Jack admitting that his friendship with his old pal was “the best choice” he ever made.

This TV show idea seems better than a previously proposed spin-off idea that came while Boy Meets World was still airing. Friedle revealed he almost left the ABC/Disney sitcom when creator Michael Jacobs pitched a “young Friends” idea for Eric to move to L.A. and meet new friends there. While it’s always amusing to see Eric’s humorous interactions, I’d rather see a straight man/funny man dynamic between him and Jack.

Now that the idea of a Jack/Eric spinoff has been brought up, this Boy Meets World fan is keeping her fingers crossed that it comes to fruition. Given that mismatched roommate shows like The Big Bang Theory, 2 Broke Girls, Perfect Strangers have been successful, why not give Jack Hunter and Eric Matthews a shot?

In the meantime, fans can watch Eric and Jack's dynamic on Boy Meets World and Girl Meets World by streaming them with a Disney+ subscription.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

#3691. Russell Brand’s Sexual Assault and Rape Scandal, Trial: Everything to Know

Russell Brand faced sexual assault, rape and emotional abuse allegations by multiple women ahead of his 2026 trial.

The U.K. newspaper The Times published a bombshell article about the actor and comedian in September 2023, in which four women alleged being sexually assaulted by Brand between the years of 2006 and 2013.

Ahead of the article’s publication — a collaboration with the Channel 4 series Dispatches —Brand denied the “very serious allegations” against him in a video posted via X.

“I’ve received two extremely disturbing letters, or a letter and an email, one from a mainstream media TV company [and] one from a newspaper, listing a litany of extremely egregious and aggressive attacks,” he explained, though did not go into detail about the claims.

Brand noted that his past “promiscuous” relationships were “absolutely, always consensual.” He added: “I was always transparent about that then — almost too transparent. And I’m being transparent about it now as well. And to see that transparency metastasized into something criminal that I absolutely deny makes me question [if] there is another agenda at play?”

Brand went on trial in fall 2026 and was convicted on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Scroll down for all the details on Russell’s sexual assault scandal and trial:

According to The Sunday Times — the Times’ sister outlet —the allegations against Brand occurred between 2006 and 2013 during his time acting in Hollywood and working as a presenter for BBC Radio 2 and Channel 4. One woman, referred to by the name Alice, accused Brand of being sexually and emotionally abusive towards her throughout their 2006 relationship, during which she was 16 years old and he was 30. She previously reported her claims to Brand’s agent, who put her in touch with his lawyer who shut down her allegations.

Another woman, identified as Nadia, claims Brand raped her in his Los Angeles home in July 2012, after which she received treatment at a rape crisis center. A third woman — Phoebe — also accused Brand of sexually assaulting her while working at his home in 2013.

Following the initial article, the outlet reported that multiple women had come forward with new allegations against Brand, prompting Parliament member Caroline Nokes to call for U.K. and U.S. police to investigate.

“This merits and needs a criminal investigation, because for too long we have seen men — and the perpetrators of these sorts of crimes are almost invariably men — not being held to account for their behaviors and their actions,” she told BBC Radio, according to Time.

The London Metropolitan Police later revealed that they were investigating a 2003 sexual assault investigation that was reported following the publication of The Times’ report.

The Thames Valley Police announced they were joining the investigation in October 2023 after a woman came forward with “new information” regarding a “harassment and stalking” report. According to the BBC, the woman previously reported her allegations several times between 2018 and 2022 but no action was taken against Brand. The comedian previously accused the woman of harassing him in 2017.

In December 2025, the former actor was accused of rape and sexual assault by two other women who alleged they had an encounter with Brand in 2009. Brand pleaded not guilty to both accusations in February 2026 while appearing in a London courtroom.

Brand later told reporters that he felt “blessed,” while photos obtained by Us at the time showed Brand carrying a bible. A hearing is scheduled for March 2026 to decide if the allegations should be included in the preexisting and ongoing case against Brand.

“I don’t mind [the media] using my books and my stand-up to talk about my promiscuous, consensual conduct in the past. What I seriously refute are these very, very serious criminal allegations,” Brand noted in his denial video, which was also uploaded to his YouTube channel. “Also, it’s worth mentioning that there are witnesses whose evidence directly contradicts the narratives that these two mainstream media outlets are trying to construct, apparently, in what seems to me to be a coordinated attack.”

He went on to state that he felt like he was “being attacked” and that he and his team were looking into the claims.

Brand subtly addressed the allegations again in a September 2023 livestream on the streaming platform Rumble. “It appears that apparently independent or at least separate news organizations are collaborating — and I hesitate to use this word — conspiring to control global news narratives in some of the most important stories in the world,” he told fans, according to Deadline.

Hours after news of the misconduct scandal broke, Brand received a standing ovation during a stand-up show at London’s Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre. After the performance, it was announced that the remaining dates of his “Bipolarisation” comedy tour had been postponed.

At the time, Deadline reported that Brand was let go from the Comedy Central series Roast Battle after one season in 2018 following accusations of being a “sexual predator” on set. Days later, the outlet revealed that the BBC and Channel 4 had removed content featuring Brand from their platforms.

“We’ve reviewed the content and made a considered decision to remove some of it, having assessed that it now falls below public expectations,” a BBC spokesperson told Deadline on Tuesday, September 19, adding, “[The BBC] does not ban or remove content when it is a matter of public record unless we have justification for doing so.”

YouTube also took action against Brand by suspending his ability to monetize content on his channel, meaning Brand can no longer earn profits from ads featured in videos.

Amid the scandal, several interviews resurfaced featuring celebrities speaking out against Brand’s previous inappropriate behavior.

His ex-wife, Katy Perry, told Vogue in 2013 that she did not want to publicly detail what led to their 2011 divorce. “I felt a lot of responsibility for it ending, but then I found out the real truth, which I can’t necessarily disclose because I keep it locked in my safe for a rainy day,” she explained. “I let go and I was like: This isn’t because of me; this is beyond me. So I have moved on from that.”

Singer Dannii Minogue — sister of pop star Kylie Minogue — called Brand a “vile predator” following her interview on his former MTV series 1 Leicester Square. “I certainly don’t think he has cured his sex addiction, that’s for sure,” she told The Mirror in 2006. “He wouldn’t take no for an answer.”

She continued: “Throughout the whole interview he kept making shocking remarks that I can’t even repeat,” adding that he also made comments about her “fabulous breasts.”

The BBC (British Broadcasting Corporation) announced via news release in November 2023 that it had received five complaints about “inappropriate behavior” demonstrated by Brand while he was working on its radio shows between 2006 and 2008. Two of the complaints were made between 2006 and 2008. Another complainant contacted the BBC in 2019, while two others came forward after the initial sexual assault allegations against Brand made headlines in September 2023.

The BBC noted that the five complaints involve “allegations of inappropriate conduct in the workplace” including “urinating in bottles in a BBC studio” and “inappropriate use of BBC cars.” Us Weekly has reached out to Brand for comment.

BBC began an inquiry into Brand’s conduct in September 2023 after news broke that several women had accused the actor of sexual assault.

According to the BBC and The Times of London, Brand was reportedly interviewed at a South London police station on November 16, 2023.

“A man in his 40s attended a police station in South London on Thursday 16 November 2023,” the Metropolitan Police shared in a written statement with People on Monday, November 20. “He was interviewed under caution by detectives in relation to three non-recent sexual offenses. Enquiries continue.”

News broke in April 2025 that the comedian was charged with rape, sexual assault and indecent assault based on allegations from four different women between 1999 and 2005.

“We have today authorized the Metropolitan Police to charge Russell Brand with a number of sexual offenses,” a spokesperson for the Crown Prosecution Service said in a statement. “We carefully reviewed the evidence after a police investigation into allegations made following the broadcast of a Channel 4 documentary in September 2023. We have concluded that Russell Brand should be charged with offenses including rape, sexual assault and indecent assault.”

Brand appeared in court in May 2025 and pleaded not guilty to the initial five charges against him. The trial was set to start in June 2026.

The Metropolitan Police confirmed in December 2025 that Brand had been charged with two more counts of rape, one count of of indecent assault and two counts of sexual assault after two more women came forward with allegations against the comedian following an alleged encounter in 2009. He pleaded not guilty to both charges in February 2026.

“The women who have made reports, including those connected to the two new charges, continue to receive support from specially trained officers,” the Metropolitan Police shared in a December 2025 statement, per Deadline. “The Met’s investigation remains ongoing, and detectives urge anyone affected by this case, or anyone with information, to come forward and speak with police.”

Brand is also facing potential criminal charges in the U.S. The Times reported on April 6 that Warner Bros. Discovery had offered to submit hours of outtakes from 2011’s Arthur, which starred Brand as the title character, as evidence in connection with an allegation of sexual assault on the film’s set.

In 2023, both Warner Bros. and Brand were sued by an extra on Arthur, identified in court documents as Jane Doe. Doe accused Brand of exposing himself to cast members before sexually assaulting her in a bathroom. Both Warner Bros. and Brand have denied the allegations.

Per The Times, Warner Bros. Discovery attorney Patrick Lamparello told a New York Supreme Court last week that the company had “some hours of video outtake footage … four or five hours, it could be more, around eight.”

Brand’s lawyer, Mark Cuccaro, said Brand had “reasonable belief criminal prosecution is possible in the U.S. based on allegations tantamount to criminal sexual misconduct occurring in the U.S., of which he has been falsely accused both by this civil plaintiff and several others through the media.”

During an April 2026 appearance on the Megyn Kelly Show, Brand admitted that he once had sex with a 16-year-old when he was 30.

“The plain fact of it is that in Europe and in the United Kingdom, where I’m from, the age of consent is 16. And I did sleep with a 16-year-old when I was 30,” he said at the time. “When I was 30, I was a very different person. I was a lot younger, and I was an immature 30-year-old.”

Brand stressed that the age of consent in the U.K. was 16, further denying any accusations of rape.

“I recognize that my sexual conduct in the past was selfish, and I did not apply enough consideration — barely any, I suppose really — to how that sex was affecting other people,” he added.

Following a two-day deliberation in November 2026, a jury at London’s Southwark Crown Court delivered a verdict on Brand’s case, finding him guilty of four of his seven charges.

He was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Brand was acquitted on two separate counts of rape and one count of an attempted indecent assault, which was reduced from indecent assault during the trial.

“Russell Brand was predatory and used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes,” senior crown prosecutor in the London Rape and Serious Sexual Assault Unit David Roberts said in a statement after court on November 5, 2026. “He was a manipulator with an insatiable desire to get what he wanted regardless of whether consent was given or not.”

Brand, for his part, mouthed, “I’m good, I’m good,” to his defense after the verdict was read, per BBC.

Brand was ultimately sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison during a hearing on November 9, 2026.

If you have experienced sexual assault, call the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 for confidential support.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way finally showed Andi Wallace and Nigel having a heart-to-heart about boundaries in their relationship, and I think it unintentionally revealed why this relationship may never work. Andi is ready for a relationship with a deep emotional connection, and it doesn't seem like Nigel is willing to do that.

TLC teased the first part of Nigel and Andi's conversation ahead of the episode, but now that we have the full context, I have thoughts. Can Nigel really be jealous of Andi texting other men, when he's seemingly unwilling to offer her anything different than what he does with all his lovers? Let's talk this out.

The latest episode of 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way to air amid the 2026 TV schedule brought up something that I'm not even sure Andi realized in the moment. While Nigel went after her for texting other men, he defended his relationships with other women as they were purely physical with limited to zero texting beyond that. Minutes later, Andi mentioned that he wouldn't text her when he's with other women, and Nigel argued that he would rarely text anyone, period.

I personally found that exchange to be telling. Since the start, I've had trouble figuring out how Nigel's relationship with Andi is different than any of his other part-time lovers. Based on their conversation about texting, I'm beginning to get the feeling that it isn't, which feels like a major problem.

90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way fans are still on the fence about whether Andi or Nigel are still together at this point. That's been even more uncertain since the revelation that Andi had been on Tinder and was embracing her side of ethical non-monogamy.

90 Day Fiancé's Angela Deem Drops Cryptic Message About Michael When Asked About Hunt For Love

I'm now wondering if the reason their relationship feels so ambiguous is due to Nigel treating Andi like she's a part-time lover. To be fair, if she ended up returning to the United States like some believe, that feels like a part-time romance. Is Nigel wrong for treating someone that way when he can only roam grocery stores with them barefoot once in a blue moon?

Also, I wouldn't be surprised if Andi realized she just wasn't going to get the emotional connection from Nigel that she desperately craved. It doesn't sound like his part-time lovers are getting that treatment either, which could just mean that it's not something he's ever going to give a partner. These two just may be a bad match, but we'll just have to wait and see.

Take-Two Interactive is one of the very few companies that, when selling four million units of something, can still get up and say that this was below forecast somehow. In an interview with IGN, Zelnick was asked why NBA 2K27 came in below expectations as reported in the company’s quarterly earnings today. In response, Zelnick said the following:

I think the key point is that while below our forecast, NBA 2K27 is our second best release of NBA 2K in history. Itâs an immensely successful title. It sold 4 million units. That said, weâre thrilled with how NBA 2K27 is performing.

This issue was addressed further in the earnings call by president Karl Slatoff, who added that the company has “seen this before on a number of different occasions” and that “it’s really hard to know exactly” why NBA 2K27 didn’t sell quite as well as Take-Two had predicted.
